shared_tips: Compare every net result with both zero-return cash and cost-matched buy-hold: relative outperformance in a falling market can still destroy capital, so never label avoided loss as profit.

Separate decision, next-close fill, and terminal mark indices: the seven-bar decision horizon here has six post-fill intervals, and collapsing those timestamps creates look-ahead and overstates attainable returns.

Report fixed nonoverlapping windows beside all overlapping prefix cases: 25 windows sharing returns are not 25 independent observations, and the four-window subset here even changes the sign of mean profit.

Keep a byte-exact executable parent and isolate only test I/O paths: this prevents accidental historical submission writes while ensuring paired comparisons measure the strategy rather than a rewritten proxy.

Treat fixed-notional sizing from the decision close as gap-risk exposure: a cash buffer is not a guarantee against a sufficiently large next-close rise; test order feasibility with fees before attributing P&L.
Do not optimize thresholds on a single fully visible 60-bar series: unchanged code with an honestly negative net result is more informative than post-hoc parameter selection without fresh validation.
